She was 36 at the time and had retired from professional tennis two years earlier.Even though Evert was no longer playing full time, tennis had not completely disappeared from her life. She had worked in broadcasting after retirement and had considered taking part in team tennis and exhibition matches. Then Alexander was born, and her plans changed.In a 1992 interview with the, Evert spoke openly about the effect her baby had on her. She said she had thought about returning to the sport while she was pregnant.But after holding Alexander in the hospital, those thoughts disappeared.“I held the baby in the hospital and after the first minute, all those feelings were gone,” Evert said.That helps explain the meaning behind her later comment about not wanting to leave his side. She had spent most of her life preparing for matches, traveling for tournaments and dealing with the pressure that came with being one of the best players in the world. Now, she had a baby who depended on her, and being there with him felt more important.The change was not about suddenly disliking tennis. Evert had simply found something that meant more to her at that stage of her life.Alexander was not just Evert’s first child. His arrival gave her a new way to measure what mattered.Before becoming a mother, much of Evert’s public life centered on tennis. She won 18 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years near the top of the sport. Winning was a huge part of her identity. Motherhood gave her a role where there was no ranking, trophy or scoreboard.Thereported in 1991 that Evert compared winning Wimbledon with having a baby. Her view was striking. A major title could bring happiness and recognition, but the feeling did not last in the same way. Having her child was something she could hold on to.“The great high of winning Wimbledon lasts for about a week,” Evert told, according to the. “But having a baby, there just isn’t any comparison.”Her words show why the birth of Alexander was such a turning point. Evert had already achieved the biggest goals in tennis. She did not need another trophy to prove what she could do. Instead, she wanted to enjoy the new part of her life that had arrived.That did not mean she stopped being Chris Evert the tennis champion. It meant she had become Chris Evert the mother too, and she was learning that the second role could bring a different kind of happiness.Alexander was the first of Evert and Andy Mill’s three sons. Nicholas was born in 1994, followed by Colton in 1996. Together, the boys became the center of a busy family life.Evert later made it clear that her feelings about motherhood had not faded as her children grew. In a 2001 interview with the, she spoke about Alexander, Nicholas and Colton while they were still young.“They’re my life, they’re the most important thing,” Evert said. “I’m busy, but I’m 100 percent a mom first.”That comment adds another layer to her earlier quote. Evert was not talking only about the excitement of having her first baby. She was describing a lasting change in how she saw herself.Her sons also grew up around sports because both of their parents were successful athletes. Still, Evert did not push them to follow the same path she had taken. She wanted them to enjoy being children instead of feeling that they had to become champions.In a later interview with, Evert again placed motherhood above her tennis achievements. Asked about the best part of being Chris Evert, she immediately pointed to her sons and being a mother.“I love my boys,” she said. “That’s been the highlight of my life.”That answer is important because it came decades after Alexander was born. Her feelings were not limited to those first few months of motherhood. They remained part of how Evert viewed her life long after her playing career had ended.Evert’s quote is simple, but it says something many parents can understand. Having a child can change what feels urgent. Things that once seemed extremely important can suddenly move down the list.For Evert, that shift came after years of living with the demands of professional tennis. She had known what it meant to spend months traveling and competing. She had also known the feeling of winning major titles in front of huge crowds.Yet when Alexander arrived, she wanted to stay close to him.That decision did not erase tennis from her life. Evert later worked as a coach, mentor and commentator, and she remained connected to the sport she had helped shape. But her relationship with tennis was different because she no longer needed to prove herself through competition.Her three sons became the part of her life she spoke about with the most pride. In 2025,again asked her about the best thing about being Chris Evert. Her answer centered on being a mother.That is why the line, “Once I had my first child, I didn’t want to leave his side,” carries more meaning than it may seem to at first. Evert was not simply describing a mother wanting to stay with her newborn. She was describing the moment her priorities changed.For a woman who had spent decades being defined by tennis, motherhood became the part of her identity she valued most. And for Evert, that change began with one child, Alexander, and the feeling that nothing else mattered quite as much as being beside him.
Article Summary: Evert became a mother on October 12, 1991, when she and her then husband, former Olympic skier Andy Mill, welcomed Alexander James Mill. The tennis great had already walked away from professional tennis when she welcomed her first son, Alexander James, in 1991. Evert later made it clear that her feelings about motherhood had not faded as her children grew up.

Article Title: Indian-origin grandmother with Green Card detained by ICE after living in the US for 30 years. Her daughter is an immigration attorney
Article Text:
Venkata Vasamsetty (middle) has been in the US for 30 years and has been a Green Card holder since 2013.

What is Venkata Vasamsetty's story?

Can a Green Card holder be arrested?

Venkata Vasamsetty, who has lived in the US for 30 years and is a Green Card holder, has been detained by ICE in a bizarre case of immigration while her daughter Yashaswini Vasamsetty is an employment-based immigration attorney licensed in Texas and New Jersey. Yashaswini's friend Zoe Ji Wilson shared the ordeal of Venkata Vasamsetty as Vasamsetty's family is collecting signatures for a 'Free Venkata' campaign.Venkata has been in the US legally for 30 years and she got her Green Card in 2013. She is a teacher with the Wake County Public School System in North Carolina, owns a house and is the mother to two daughters, who are US citizens. She is also a grandmother to US citizens. The family said that Venkata does not have any criminal records and not even a speeding ticket ever.Yes, a Green Card holder can be arrested if they break the conditions that one needs to fulfil as a Green Card holder. An absence of more than six months from the US can raise questions about whether a permanent resident intended to abandon their US residence. This happened in Vasamsetty's case during a Covid emergency.In July 2022, Venkata traveled to India to see her father, who was suffering from several medical conditions.She got COVID in November and had to defer her return to the US as she had to be hospitalized in India for nearly two weeks. She returned to the US in February 2023 -- after spending seven months outside the US.She was stopped at the Raleigh-Durham International Airport as she returned and the DHS told her that she had been abroad for a long period, which made a case of intention to abandon the Green Card. But she was, at that time, in the process of purchasing a house in North Carolina and had no intention of going back to India.ICE gave her a date to appear in immigration court and allowed her to go home to her family for the time being. She was asked to report to ICE’s Charlotte office on a regular basis. Her family said that Venkata attended every single ICE appointment and they submitted all the documents to prove that it was only the situation that delayed her and she had no intention to leave the US.A court then finally ordered in favour of Venkata and said that the DHS could not meet their "burden of proving by clear and convincing evidence" that Vasamsetty was removable as charged.On May 19, 2026, the case against Vasamsetty was terminated and she was moved out of the removal proceedings. But she had a scheduled ICE appointment on July 11. ICE did not cancel the date and Vasamsetty did not skip the appointment either assuming that she did not have any need to appear as the case ws dropped. She took the court order to the appointment but she was asked to come a month later as ICE did not have its records updated. When she went for the August 11 appointment, she was detained.Vasamsetty was taken to Irwin County Detention Center in Ocilla, Georgia."No warning. No notice. No opportunity to prepare. No regard for the fact that an Immigration Judge had already terminated her removal proceedings. No regard for the fact that she is severely diabetic and did not have her insulin, medications, or medical supplies with her. No regard for any of that. They put her in handcuffs and took her into custody. DHS did not file a new Notice to Appear until the day after she was detained. She was not in proceedings at the time of her arrest," Wilson wrote in her post."If this can happen to Yesh's mother, people need to understand what this means. It means lawful status, decades of compliance, a clean record, a court order, and even basic medical vulnerability may still not be enough to protect someone from being detained and stripped of their freedom. That should terrify all of us," Wilson wrote noting that not everyone has lawyers in their families.
Article Summary: Venkata Vasamsetty has been in the US legally for 30 years and she got her Green Card in 2013. She is a teacher with the Wake County Public School System in North Carolina, owns a house and is the mother to two daughters, who are US citizens. The family said that Venkata does not have any criminal records and not even a speeding ticket ever.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates: "A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman. But the search to find that voice…" - a powerful lesson on confidence and strength
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates

Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates

"A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman. But the search to find that voice can be remarkably difficult"

What Melinda French Gates actually said, in her own fuller words

What is the meaning behind this quote by Melinda Gates

Why finding your own voice is genuinely so difficult for so many people

Why having a real voice is about far more than simply being loud

Why confidence and having a real voice are so closely connected

Why women in particular can face additional barriers here

Why speaking up can genuinely create real change

Why finding your voice never actually requires having every answer

Other famous quotes by Melinda French Gates

"Women and girls should be able to determine their own future, no matter where they're born."

"If you invest in a girl or a woman, you are investing in everybody else."

"Helping people doesn't have to be an unsound financial strategy."

"That is why we women have to lift each other up, not to replace men at the top of the hierarchy, but to become partners with men in ending hierarchy."

Why this quote is relevant today

Melinda French Gates' words speak to something a great many people quietly recognise in themselves, the long, often uncomfortable journey towards genuine confidence, honest self-expression, and standing up for whatever actually matters to you. "A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman," she said. "But the search to find that voice can be remarkably difficult." She said this in a speech delivered on 16 October 2003, at the Powerful Voices Luncheon in Seattle, an organisation supporting girls and young women in the region, and the full transcript remains available today on the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation's own website. Speaking with genuine confidence rarely comes naturally to everyone straight away, and for a great many women in particular, finding that voice in the first place can genuinely mean working through real fear, real social expectation, and the quiet pressure to simply stay agreeable and stay quiet instead.The full passage from that 2003 speech gives the quote considerably more depth than the single line usually shared on its own. "How does a girl become strong? How does she enact change? How does she grow into a strong woman?" Gates asked her audience directly. "It begins with a step that sounds simple, but isn't. She finds her voice. A woman with a voice is by definition a strong woman. But the search to find that voice can be remarkably difficult." She went on to name real, specific reasons why that search is genuinely so hard, pointing out that in most nations around the world, women still receive substantially less education than men, and that in much of the developing world, most women do not receive any formal education at all. She then added something even more pointed, that finding one's voice "is made more difficult by the thousands of subtle pressures, covert and overt, that coax young women to mute their voices in order to please their parents, their teachers, their boyfriends and sometimes even their employers."The quote suggests that having a genuine voice is really about a good deal more than simply being able to speak out loud. It means feeling confident enough to actually express your own ideas, your own boundaries, your own honest beliefs, even when doing so feels genuinely uncomfortable. Building that kind of confidence takes real time for almost everyone. People very often already know exactly what they think, yet still hesitate to say it out loud, worried about criticism, rejection, or simply being judged unfairly for speaking up. Social expectation shapes how comfortable someone actually feels about speaking openly too, sometimes in ways that are genuinely hard to notice until you stop and look closely at your own hesitation. Finding your own voice, in this sense, becomes a genuinely personal journey rather than a single moment that simply happens to you. It often requires patience, self-awareness and the willingness to accept that not everyone will understand or agree with what you have to say.Confidence never develops in quite the same way for everyone. Someone might grow up somewhere that actively discourages questioning authority of any kind. Someone else might have lived through real situations where their own honest opinion was repeatedly dismissed or ignored outright. Others simply worry, quietly and constantly, about saying the wrong thing at the wrong moment. Experiences like these can gradually make staying silent feel genuinely safer than actually speaking up. Finding your voice, in the end, really means learning to move past that accumulated fear, and properly recognising that your own perspective genuinely has value worth sharing.Being genuinely heard was never really about speaking the loudest in the room. A strong, real voice can be calm, considered and genuinely thoughtful just as easily as it can be forceful. It can mean saying no clearly, asking a genuinely difficult question nobody else wants to ask, sharing an unpopular honest opinion, or simply speaking up the moment something feels unfair to you. Real strength comes from a genuine willingness to express yourself honestly, not from dominating every single conversation you happen to be part of.Confidence certainly makes it easier to communicate what you actually want and genuinely believe. Confidence does not always have to arrive first, though, however much it might feel that way from the outside. Very often it develops precisely because someone begins using their own voice in the first place, however tentatively at first. The very first time someone speaks up in a genuinely difficult situation can feel deeply uncomfortable. The next time, though, tends to feel just slightly easier than the last, and those small, repeated experiences gradually build into something closer to real, lasting confidence over time.Gates' quote focuses specifically on women and the particular challenges genuinely involved in finding their own voice. Women often face real social expectations around exactly how they should behave, communicate and respond, both professionally and personally, and being assertive can sometimes be judged very differently depending entirely on who happens to be speaking at the time. That creates a genuinely difficult balance between wanting to express an honest opinion and worrying constantly about how that opinion will actually be received by other people. Recognising these real pressures honestly is part of understanding exactly why finding one's own voice can genuinely take so long for so many women.A voice becomes particularly powerful the moment it gets used to draw real attention to something that genuinely needs to change. Speaking honestly about an unfair experience can encourage other people to finally share their own. Raising a genuine concern at work can lead directly to a better process for everyone involved. One person's simple willingness to speak up can sometimes make it considerably easier for other people around them to finally do the same.People sometimes stay silent because they wrongly believe they need to be completely certain about something before they are allowed to speak at all. Expressing a genuine opinion has never actually required perfect knowledge though. It can be as simple as saying "I see this differently," or "I don't understand," or "I think there might be another way." Asking a genuine question, in fact, can often be just as powerful as making a confident statement outright.Finding your own voice remains one of the genuinely important steps toward real confidence and independence, whether that means speaking up in a meeting, challenging an assumption you know is unfair, expressing a genuine personal boundary, or simply telling someone exactly what you think. That whole process can feel genuinely uncomfortable, especially after years spent quietly worrying about how other people might respond. Gates' message is really a reminder that strength does not always have to begin with confidence already fully formed. Sometimes real confidence only begins the moment you decide that your own voice actually deserves to be heard in the first place. Finding that voice can genuinely take time, but once you actually do, it has a way of quietly changing both how you see yourself, and how everyone else around you sees you too.
Article Summary: Melinda French Gates gave the quote in a speech in Seattle in 2003. The full transcript of the speech is available on the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation's own website. The quote suggests that having a genuine voice is about more than simply being able to speak out loud.

Article Title: Ballon d’Or winner Rodri demands Barcelona star give up No. 16 shirt he wore at Man City and Spain
Article Text:
Spain's Rodri (16) celebrates after winning the World Cup Group H soccer match between Uruguay and Spain in Zapopan, near Guadalajara, Mexico, Friday, June 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Ricardo Mazalan)

No. 16

Why Rodri wanted No. 16

Spain's Rodri poses with the tournament's best player award at the end of the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Fermín moves to No. 7

Barcelona's major move for Rodri

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rodri is closing in on his move to Barcelona, and one of his first requests at his new club has involved a shirt number that has followed him through some of the biggest moments of his career.The Spain international has asked to wearat Barcelona, the number he has worn throughout his Manchester City career and with Spain. With Fermín López previously occupying the shirt, the Catalan club have now made room for Rodri by moving the midfielder to No. 7.The connection between Rodri and the number goes back well beyond his impending arrival at Barcelona. He selected No. 16 when he joined Manchester City from Atlético Madrid in 2019 and kept it throughout his seven-year spell in England.It has also become his established number with Spain, including during the country's run to the 2026 World Cup title. Rodri captained Spain as they beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time and was named the tournament's Golden Ball winner.That came after he had already established himself as one of the defining midfielders of his generation at club level. His performances for Manchester City helped him win four Premier League titles and the Champions League, while his form with Spain at Euro 2024 contributed to him becoming the first defensive midfielder to win the Ballon d'Or since its modern voting era began.So when Barcelona became his next destination, Rodri wanted to keep the number that had become closely associated with him.According to Fabrizio Romano, Rodri has asked to wear No. 16 at Barcelona during his conversations with Fermín López over recent days. Fermín is set to switch to No. 7, allowing Rodri to retain his familiar number.The number had belonged to Fermín López, but the timing of the change worked in Barcelona's favour.Ferran Torres left the club for Paris Saint-Germain in a €50 million ($57.8 million) transfer, leaving the No. 7 shirt vacant. Fermín has now taken that number, while his move frees No. 16 for Rodri.The switch also gives Fermín a number with considerable history at Barcelona. The No. 7 has previously been worn by players including David Villa, Pedro, Ousmane Dembélé and Antoine Griezmann.For Rodri, meanwhile, there is no adjustment required. He arrives in Catalonia with the same number that has accompanied him through his most successful years.The shirt-number change comes as Barcelona prepare to complete one of the biggest transfers of their summer.Barcelona and Manchester City have reached an agreement in principle for Rodri, with the package reported at €76.5 million ($88.4 million). The Spanish champions had seen two earlier offers rejected before returning with a third proposal that City accepted. Rodri is expected to sign a four-year contract.The move brings the 30-year-old back to Spain after seven trophy-filled seasons in England. Rodri made 298 appearances for City and won 12 major honours, including four Premier League titles, two FA Cups, three EFL Cups and the Champions League.His arrival also addresses an immediate midfield need for Barcelona, with Frenkie de Jong's injury having forced the club to look for additional quality in the position. Rodri's ability to control games from the base of midfield gives Hansi Flick an experienced option alongside a group that includes Pedri, Gavi, Dani Olmo and Fermín.Barcelona are also bringing back João Cancelo, who is set to return as a free agent after terminating his contract with Al Hilal, while Rodri's arrival reunites him with several Spanish players and gives the club another player with experience of winning at the highest level.Rodri is expected to arrive in Barcelona before completing his medical, with the club considering a presentation at the Camp Nou during the Joan Gamper Trophy against Al Hilal.And when he eventually walks out in Barcelona colours, it appears the shirt will look familiar: No. 16, just as it has been throughout the most important chapters of his career.
Article Summary: Rodri has asked to wear No. 16 at Barcelona, the number he has worn throughout his Manchester City career and with Spain. With Fermín López previously occupying the shirt, the Catalan club have now made room for Rodri by moving the midfielder to No. 7.

Article Title: Legendary Wolves captain and former England star Mike Bailey dies aged 84 after long dementia battle
Article Text:
Wolves icon Mike Bailey dies aged 84 after dementia battle

Bailey's Wolves career

'One of Wolves' greatest ever captains'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From Molineux captain to management

Wolverhampton Wanderers legend Mike Bailey has died aged 84 following a long battle with dementia, bringing an end to the career of a player who captained the club through one of the most important periods in its history.Bailey spent 11 years at Molineux between 1966 and 1977, making 436 appearances and scoring 25 goals. He also won two England caps, having represented his country in 1964.Bailey had been diagnosed with dementia in 2017. According to ExpressAndStar.com, his family revealed his battle with the degenerative condition in an interview with the outlet six years ago, saying they believed years of heading footballs throughout his life had contributed to it.His death was announced as former Wolves team-mates and supporters were already mourning the loss of another Molineux great, Phil Parkes, who died earlier this month.Bailey joined Wolves in 1966 and during his first full season was part of the side that won promotion back to the top division in 1967. He was named Midlands Player of the Year that season and went on to become one of the defining figures of the team during the club's revival in English football in the 1960s and 1970s.Wolves reached the Uefa Cup final in 1972 with Bailey as a key figure, although they were beaten 3-2 by Tottenham Hotspur in an all-English final.Two years later, Bailey finally lifted a major trophy with Wolves when he captained the side to a 2-1 League Cup final victory over Manchester City at the old Wembley Stadium. Wolves described it as his “finest afternoon at the club”.The club paid tribute to Bailey in its official statement, highlighting the qualities that made him such an important figure at Molineux.“During that popular Wolves stint, Bailey was known by those on the Molineux terraces for his love of a tackle, creative passing and eye for the occasional spectacular strike, but more than all that, his leadership,” the club said.John Richards, the former Wolves goalscorer and chairman of the Wolves Former Players' Association, paid tribute to Bailey as “one of Wolves’ greatest ever captains”.“Coming so soon after the passing of Lofty (Phil Parkes), who was one of Mike’s close pals within our team, this is another devastating loss,” Richards said.“I can’t fully describe how much respect I have for Mike as a player and as a person.“His influence on us as players, both with his leadership and his performances, is something that made him such a massive part of the dressing room.“He was a great captain, not only in how he led the team but also the individual pieces of advice and guidance he gave to each of us as players.”Richards also recalled what it meant to see Bailey lift the League Cup at Wembley after such a long career without a major trophy.“When we won the League Cup final in 1974, with Mike as captain, we were all just as pleased for him as we were for ourselves because, up until then, he had gone through such an incredible career without lifting a trophy,” Richards said.“To see him go up there at Wembley and lift the trophy is one of my greatest ever Wolves memories.”Richards said Bailey remained connected to the club long after his playing career ended, regularly returning to Wolverhampton for matches and events and later serving as chairman of the former players’ association.“In recent years, he responded to illness with the same courage and determination as he displayed during his football career, and we send all our best wishes and condolences to Barbara, Victoria, Andy and the family,” Richards said.“Wolves has lost one of its greatest ever captains, but his achievements and influence will never be forgotten.”Bailey left Wolves in 1977 after 11 years at the club and continued playing in the United States with Minnesota Kicks before returning to England for one final season with Hereford. He retired from playing in 1979 and subsequently moved into management.His managerial career included spells with Hereford, Charlton, Brighton, Greek club OFI and Leatherhead, extending his involvement in football well beyond his playing days.For Wolves, however, Bailey's legacy remained rooted in the period when he led the club on the pitch, from promotion back to the top division through European competition and ultimately to the League Cup triumph at Wembley.
Article Summary: Wolverhampton Wanderers legend Mike Bailey has died aged 84 following a long battle with dementia. Bailey spent 11 years at Molineux between 1966 and 1977, making 436 appearances and scoring 25 goals. He also won two England caps, having represented his country in 1964 and 1964. Bailey captained the club through one of the most important periods in its history.

Article Title: How Von Miller can help the Cowboys’ pass rush? Eight-time Pro Bowler brings veteran experience as Dallas revamps its defensive front
Article Text:
How Von Miller can help the Cowboys’ pass rush? Eight-time pro bowler brings veteran experience as Dallas revamps its defensive front(Getty)

Von Miller gives the Dallas Cowboys another proven pass-rush option

Von Miller can help Dallas develop its young pass rush

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Von Miller gives the Dallas Cowboys a proven pass rusher at a time when their defense needs more pressure. Dallas officially added the eight-time Pro Bowler after Miller led the Washington Commanders with nine sacks in 2025. At 37, he no longer carries the workload of his prime, but his recent production shows he can still make quarterbacks uncomfortable.That makes Miller an interesting piece for Dallas rather than a player who needs to carry the defense. The Cowboys can use his experience in passing situations while allowing younger edge rushers to handle larger roles. If Miller stays productive in a focused role, his addition could give Dallas a useful boost throughout the 2026 season.The clearest reason for optimism comes from what Miller did last season. He played all 17 games for Washington in 2025 and started only three, yet he still finished with nine sacks. That total led the Commanders and marked his highest single-season sack total since 2018. He also reached that number while playing a limited role, which makes his fit with the Cowboys particularly interesting.Dallas needs that kind of production. The Cowboys finished tied for 22nd in the NFL with 35 sacks in 2025 after trading Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers last August.The defense also needs to replace the production it lost from Jadeveon Clowney, who led Dallas with 8.5 sacks before leaving for Houston. Miller already has a recent season in which he produced more sacks than Clowney did for the Cowboys.The Cowboys also have other pieces around Miller. Rashan Gary gives Dallas an established veteran presence, while Donovan Ezeiruaku enters his second season and first-round pick Malachi Lawrence gives the group another young option. That setup should allow Dallas to avoid putting too much responsibility on Miller.Instead, the Cowboys can pick the spots where his experience matters most. Third downs, two-minute situations and late-game passing downs could give Miller opportunities to attack quarterbacks without forcing him into an oversized workload.His career numbers also explain why his presence matters. Miller enters his 15th NFL season with 138.5 sacks, the most among active players and tied for ninth in NFL history. He has played 203 regular-season games, won two Super Bowls and earned Super Bowl 50 MVP honors with Denver.Miller's value should extend beyond the sack column because the Cowboys have several younger players who still need to establish themselves. His experience can give Dallas another reliable veteran voice while those players take on larger responsibilities.The move also brings a personal connection. Miller grew up in Texas and played college football at Texas A&M before the Denver Broncos selected him No. 2 overall in the 2011 NFL Draft. On Aug. 16, he confirmed his move to Dallas on Instagram with the message, “Hereee Weee Gooo @dallascowboys LFG!!!”Miller has not made a Pro Bowl since 2019, so Dallas cannot expect the dominant version of the player who once terrorized offensive tackles every week. However, his nine sacks last season provide a much better indicator of what he can offer now.For the Cowboys, that is enough to make this move meaningful. Miller does not have to become the old Von Miller. He simply needs to provide timely pressure, veteran know-how and another problem for opposing quarterbacks. If he does that, Dallas could get exactly what its rebuilt pass rush needs.
Article Summary: Von Miller is an eight-time Pro Bowler. He has played 203 regular-season games, won two Super Bowls and earned Super Bowl 50 MVP honors with Denver. The Cowboys can use his experience in passing situations while allowing younger edge rushers to handle larger roles.

Article Title: From Charles Haley to Von Miller: “Flawed individuals are some of my greatest role models” - Jerry Jones-led Dallas Cowboys’ history of taking chances on controversial stars
Article Text:
From Charles Haley to Von Miller: “Flawed individuals are some of my greatest role models” - Jerry Jones-led Dallas Cowboys’ history of taking chances on controversial stars(Image via X: Charles Haley and Von Miller​)

Jerry Jones-led Cowboys’ attraction to signing troubled past or controversial players like Charles Haley in 1992 and Von Miller in 2026

Von Miller’s controversial past includes a domestic violence case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jerry Jones said in Netflix’s America’s Team: The Gambler and His Cowboys that the physical and mental aspects of football are very complicated.“You’ve even heard it said, ‘You can’t play football successfully with Sunday school teachers.’ So, if you wait around and try to get the player with the perfect character, you’ve given yourself a handicap that’s not necessary. In fact, flawed individuals are some of my greatest role models,” Jones said.Charles Haley was known to scare coaches, while Von Miller has a troubled past, including a domestic violence case involving his then-girlfriend in 2023. Let’s check out these flawed individuals who were/can be rehabilitated, according to Jerry Jones.Charles Haley was a Pro Bowl player who had won two Super Bowls. The only problem he had was the horror stories coaches had heard about him.The legendary defensive end came with a troubled past of scolding coaches, being aggressive, and, plain and simple, being the torchbearer of horror stories.Haley himself admitted on Netflix’s America’s Team: The Gambler and His Cowboys that he has three personalities within himself – Chuck [the a*sh*le], Charlie [the sensitive one who cries all the time], and Charles [the sensible one].“Let me give you a secret: whatever came into my head, I did. I didn’t give a sh*t,” he said.“Charles always found a rookie to pick on,” Bill Romanowski said on Netflix’s America’s Team: The Gambler and His Cowboys. “When I got to the 49ers, I happened to be that rookie. You know, calling me a ‘p*ssy.’Then in 1992, I heard that Charles walked up into the general manager’s office; he pulled out his d*ck, pissed on his desk, and said, ‘This is how bad I want out of here.’”Jerry Jones admitted that it was “dicey” bringing Charles Haley from the San Francisco 49ers, but Jones is a huge believer in rehabilitation. So, he took the risk. And they won a Super Bowl that year! Not just one, but three! With Haley playing for them.Could this happen with Von Miller? He also comes with a troubled past. He also has two Super Bowls. He also happens to be an edge rusher! Can we stop here? Maybe not…Court documents obtained by WFAA in November 2023 reported that Von Miller was accused of assaulting his then-pregnant girlfriend at their high-rise apartment in Dallas.When police officers arrived at the scene, they found “minor abrasions” on Miller’s longtime girlfriend’s hand and bruising on her neck – “injuries consistent with applied pressure to the neck.”According to the arrest warrant affidavit, Miller and his girlfriend were arguing in their bedroom because she did not want to travel on her birthday that week. When the alleged victim went from the bedroom to the office, she slammed the office door in rage. This made Miller visibly angry.He went into the office and yelled at his girlfriend to “get out” of the apartment. The girlfriend began to comply with Miller’s request and attempted to gather her belongings when Miller began to shove and push her, all while telling her to leave the apartment.He then began to film her on his phone while continuing to push and shove her out of the home. She kept yelling, “Stop! I’m pregnant.” But Miller kept pushing. Then Miller applied pressure around the girlfriend’s neck for three to five seconds before letting go.The 911 call had her saying, “My boyfriend is choking and hitting me… I have bruises all over me, my hair is out.”When the dispatcher asked her about the boyfriend, she said, “He just stormed out.” The dispatcher then asked her if she needed paramedics; she said, “I don’t know. He pulled my hair out. I have, like, some blood on me… but not like…Yeah, I don’t know.”A warrant for a third-degree felony charge of assaulting a pregnant person was issued for Miller in November 2023, when he played for the Buffalo Bills.Miller turned himself in and was taken to the DeSoto Police Department jail for processing. He immediately posted a $5,000 bond and was released.Fast forward to today: the Dallas Cowboys have signed him for the 2026 season. Jerry Jones’ belief in rehabilitation is so strong; can this hypothetical modern-day Charles Haley lead the Cowboys to a Super Bowl win? Especially after a 30-year drought? Remains to be seen…

Article Title: Ravindra Jadeja scripts history with 350th Test wicket, joins Kapil, Botham, Vettori in elite club
Article Text:
Ravindra Jadeja (AP Photo)

Jadeja joins Kapil, Botham and Vettori

Another milestone in an extraordinary career

Poll Vote & Share your view Who do you believe was the most influential all-rounder among Jadeja, Kapil Dev, Botham, and Vettori? Kapil Dev Ian Botham Daniel Vettori Ravindra Jadeja 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Ravindra Jadeja added another remarkable milestone to his Test career on Monday, becoming only the fourth cricketer in history to score at least 4,000 runs and take 350 or more wickets in the longest format.Jadeja reached the landmark on the third day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, picking up his second wicket of the innings to complete 350 Test wickets. His milestone wicket came when Keshara Nuwantha attempted to slap-drive an away-turner through the off side, only for the ball to take a deflection off his knee and balloon towards Shubman Gill , who completed the catch.The wicket also made Jadeja only the fifth Indian to reach 350 Test wickets, joining Anil Kumble (619), Ravichandran Ashwin (537), Kapil Dev (434) and Harbhajan Singh (417).Jadeja had earlier scored 13 runs in India's first innings, which ended on 462, before making his mark with the ball as Sri Lanka reached 243/7 in reply.Jadeja's latest achievement puts him in an exclusive club alongside three legendary all-rounders — Kapil Dev, Ian Botham and Daniel Vettori.Kapil remains the leading run-scorer among the four, having amassed 5,248 runs and taken 434 wickets in 131 Tests for India.England great Botham finished with 5,200 runs and 383 wickets in 102 Tests, while former New Zealand captain Vettori collected 4,531 runs and 362 wickets in 113 Tests.Jadeja, with 4,108 runs and 350 wickets in 90 Tests, is the only member of the elite quartet to have achieved the double before playing 100 Tests, underlining the extraordinary efficiency of his all-round contribution.The milestone further strengthens Jadeja's standing among the most productive left-arm spinners in Test history. He is now third among left-arm spinners for Test wickets, behind Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath (433) and Vettori (362), while England's Derek Underwood (297) and Bangladesh's Taijul Islam (271) follow.Jadeja's consistency with both bat and ball has made him one of India's most valuable Test cricketers over the past decade. His ability to contribute runs down the order while providing control and wickets as a spinner has repeatedly allowed India to balance their playing XI.Among left-arm spinners with at least 125 Test wickets, only South Africa's Keshav Maharaj has a better strike rate than Jadeja's 58.1, with Maharaj at 56.4.The 350-wicket mark also places Jadeja alongside some of the game's most celebrated all-rounders, but his route to the milestone stands apart. While Kapil, Botham and Vettori crossed 4,000 runs and 350 wickets after lengthy Test careers, Jadeja has reached the same landmark in fewer than 100 matches.With the first Test against Sri Lanka still in progress, Jadeja now has the opportunity to add to both his wicket and run tallies and further cement his place among Test cricket's greatest all-rounders.
Article Summary: Jadeja becomes fourth cricketer in history to score at least 4,000 runs and take 350 or more wickets in the longest format. Jadeja reached the landmark on the third day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, picking up his second wicket of the innings to complete 350 wickets.

Article Title: Super Bowl LXI lands on Valentine’s Day for the first time in history creating an unusual football-versus-romance showdown
Article Text:
Super Bowl LXI (Getty Images)

Super Bowl LXI and Valentine’s Day create a unique clash

Super Bowl 2027 brings another major change for NFL fans

Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL ’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine’s Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. With romance and football competing for the same Sunday, fans have already begun joking about dinner reservations, watch parties and the ultimate relationship compromise.The date alone is enough to make the 2027 Super Bowl stand out. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, meaning couples will have to decide how they want to spend one of the biggest nights on the American sporting calendar.For football fans, the answer may seem obvious. For couples with different priorities, however, the evening could require some negotiation.Social media has already embraced the idea. One Reddit commenter joked about the pressure on restaurants, writing:"The Valentine's Day brunch reservations are going to be harder to get than a Super Bowl ticket."Another post took the joke even further, imagining the holiday as a test of romantic loyalty:"Super Bowl on Valentine's? Peak relationship apocalypse incoming—guys choosing touchdowns over touchy-feely dates. Ladies, demand a halftime proposal or it's single season next year."The humor works because the conflict is so easy to imagine. A romantic dinner could overlap with pregame coverage. A reservation might clash with kickoff.And anyone hosting a Super Bowl party could suddenly find themselves planning around Valentine's Day expectations.There is also a convenient escape route. The game falls on Presidents' Day weekend, giving many people the chance to turn the occasion into a longer celebration. Couples could celebrate Valentine's Day on Saturday, watch the Super Bowl on Sunday and use Monday to recover from the late night.The unusual date is not the only reason Super Bowl LXI will be significant. ESPN will broadcast the championship game for the first time in network history, with ABC also carrying the event. ESPN has already outlined extensive programming and storytelling designed to build anticipation well before the game itself.The timing also feeds into a broader conversation about the Super Bowl calendar. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday, particularly because fans already tend to treat Presidents' Day weekend as a natural extension of Super Bowl celebrations.Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously discussed how changes to the NFL schedule could eventually push the Super Bowl toward Presidents' Day weekend. In comments cited in the original report, he said:"I think if you went to 18 weeks regular season that would probably occur," Goodell said at the time. "It is possible somewhere in the calendar. Could happen before that just because of the calendar, the way it lays out.But I think 18 weeks would get you to that point, and I think it would be a really great move."For now, February 14, 2027 remains a one-of-a-kind collision between football and romance. The NFL has confirmed the date, and fans have plenty of time to decide whether Super Bowl Sunday will be a date-night disaster, a couples' tradition or simply the perfect excuse to order wings and watch football together.
Article Summary: Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine's Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday.

Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC, while Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.But there is a big gap, and public net-worth numbers are best seen as estimates, not audited financial statements. Lesnar’s contracts in the modern era, UFC purses and limited-appearance model allowed him to make individual paydays that were much larger than what was generally available to wrestlers during Flair’s peak years. Meanwhile, Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling-related projects, despite the financial difficulties that have beset his wealth over the years.Brock Lesnar seems to be in a better financial state at the moment. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his net worth at $10 million, whereas NDTV reported an estimate of $17 million in June 2026. Other outlets have published higher numbers, a testament to the uncertainties that come with calculating celebrity net worth.Ric Flair is worth much less. His net worth has been estimated to be $500,000 by Celebrity Net Worth, but other estimates online have put the figure at a much higher number.The variation reflects the absence of publicly verified personal financial records, and the challenge of calculating assets, liabilities, royalties and ongoing income for a longtime entertainer.Lesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. He was an instant star in WWE after debuting in 2002, but he later moved away from the wrestling world to try his hand at the NFL and mixed martial arts before returning to WWE as an established crossover star.Lesnar’s career in WWE has been as much about scarcity as it has been about star power. He was often employed on a limited schedule around major storylines and premium live events for most of his later career instead of working weekly.Lesnar’s UFC career distinguished his money story from most WWE stars. After leaving professional wrestling, he came into MMA and immediately became a big draw. Beating Randy Couture for the heavyweight championship at UFC 91 made him a legit heavyweight champion and gave him a serious bump in commercial appeal.Lesnar has also earned money from endorsements and appearances. Jimmy John’s and other commercial deals are among his previous endorsement deals, and his celebrity status has helped his value outside the ring.He has also kept his lifestyle very private. Recent reports have pointed out that he prefers a rural lifestyle and owning vast amounts of land, rather than the high-profile celebrity lifestyle that many sports stars enjoy.Ric Flair’s financial story started in an era when the economics of professional wrestling were very different. The Nature Boy became one of the defining stars of the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE, headlining big events and winning championships through a career that spanned several decades.Flair made a ton of money in his time with WCW. One published estimate puts his WCW earnings from 1996-2000 at about $1.95 million. But the size of his earnings did not translate directly into lasting wealth because of taxes, legal obligations, medical expenses and other financial pressures.He also made a lot of money from his WWE career. Flair was a wrestler, manager and personality and stayed a close associate of the company for years. In 2005, during a divorce hearing, it was revealed that his annual WWE salary was reportedly around $500,000, showing how much he could make from wrestling even later in his career.Of the two stars, Flair's financial history is the starkest contrast. Celebrity Net Worth states that in 2000, the IRS filed a lien of more than $870,000 against him, and his further tax problems damaged his finances. The same source reports that in 2019 there was a major medical emergency that resulted in a medical bill of approximately $1.8 million.These pressures help explain why lifetime earnings and current net worth can look so dramatically different. Making millions in a career doesn’t always translate to keeping millions after taxes, debts, medical expenses and other costs.Lesnar’s future financial prospects will probably continue to be linked to his standing as a top-tier combat sports attraction. As his active wrestling career is changing, his name still has value for special appearances, merchandise, licensing and media projects.Flair’s earning model is a unique one. At 77, his money-making opportunities are increasingly linked to his legacy rather than regular ring competition. He still turns up at wrestling events, signs autographs and does other promotional stuff.Lesnar has a path to victory in the modern economics of sports and one of the rare WWE-to-UFC crossover careers. Flair’s financial legacy isn’t so much the wealth he has today, but the incredible value he brought to pro wrestling in terms of sales. Their careers demonstrate two different paths a wrestling superstar can take to earn money: Lesnar with premium modern contracts and crossover sports earnings, and Flair with longevity, character, championships and lasting brand recognition.
Article Summary: Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC. Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.

Article Title: “I just want to share that with all these little kids”: How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need
Article Text:
How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need(Getty)

Sophie Cunningham turned her WNBA fines joke into a $10,182 act of kindness

Sophie Cunninghum past Ronald McDonald House connection goes back to 2015

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sophie Cunningham had plenty of reasons to be frustrated in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard picked up multiple WNBA fines before a knee injury ended her season early. But a joke she made during that stretch took an unexpected turn. What started as a GoFundMe for fines or even a yacht raised $10,182. Cunningham then chose to give the money to a cause that had already touched her life.On Oct. 2, 2025, Sophie Cunningham launched a GoFundMe with a $26,000 goal. The Indiana Fever guard kept things playful when she explained the reason behind it.“This is more of a joke than anything. For fines only or to charity or for a yacht idk…,” Cunningham wrote on the GoFundMe page.The joke quickly caught on with her supporters. Over the next five days, 171 people donated to the fundraiser. Contributions ranged from $5 to $2,699, and the total eventually reached $10,182.That was when Cunningham decided the money would take a different path. “A yacht would be nice, but whatever we raise here will be going directly to Ronald McDonald House Charities. I’ll take care of my own fines. Y’all are the best,” Cunningham wrote in an update on the GoFundMe page, according to the Indianapolis Star's Oct.10, 2025 report.The decision came after a season in which Cunningham had become increasingly vocal about her frustrations with the WNBA. She had received multiple fines after speaking publicly about league officiating.In an August episode of her podcast, Show Me Something, Sophie Cunningham explained her disciplinary record with a joke of her own.“I’m officially 3-for-3 on being fined by the WNBA,” she said during the episode.She also explained why she continued to speak out, saying, “I promise you, everyone in our league feels that way and I’m just kind of the only one who says something.”So the fundraiser made sense at the moment. Sophie Cunningham had joked about the fines, fans responded and the money started coming in. Yet when she had more than $10,000 sitting in the fundraiser, she did not use it to erase the fines that had inspired the idea.Instead, she picked Ronald McDonald House Charities. That choice also came during a difficult personal stretch. Cunningham's 2025 season ended on Aug. 17 after she tore the MCL in her right knee. She later spent time on the sideline alongside several injured Fever teammates, including Caitlin Clark and Sydney Colson.During the Fever's exit interviews, Cunningham made it clear that she planned to return strong. When reporters asked whether she expected to be healthy for the 2026 season, she answered, “Hell yeah, man,” before saying she hoped to ramp up basketball activities in January.The fundraiser gave Cunningham a chance to do something positive while she waited for her own return.The charity was not just any random act. Sophie Cunningham first encountered Ronald McDonald House Charities as a teenager.Ronald McDonald House Charities helps families stay close to their children while they receive medical treatment. Its programmes provide places to stay, meals and other support for families facing difficult medical situations. Cunningham’s donation therefore went toward a cause that helps families during some of the hardest moments of their lives.On 2015, the Columbia Missourian reported on Cunningham's visit to a Ronald McDonald House in Chicago while she prepared for the McDonald's All-American Game. She met Brian and Jennifer Godish and their four-year-old son, Bradley, who had leukemia. Cunningham played with Bradley, built wooden train tracks with him and joined other children for basketball. She also volunteered to visit children who could not leave the hospital.“It makes me smile because this is how my parents raised me, and I’m just a little bit of who they are. I just want to share that with all these little kids and their parents,” Cunningham told the Columbia Missourian during that 2015 visit.Ten years later, she was once again giving to the same organisation. This time, her fans helped her raise the money.What began as a joke about WNBA fines ended with Sophie Cunningham choosing kindness over keeping the money for herself, adding a meaningful chapter to a connection that started long before her Indiana Fever career.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham started a GoFundMe page to raise money for fines or a yacht. The Indiana Fever guard then chose to give the money to Ronald McDonald House Charities. Cunningham first encountered the charity as a teenager during a McDonald's All-American Game.

Allen brings much more NHL experience, while Rittich has also spent years in the league. Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting
Article Text:
Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting

What did Naomi Osaka mean when she said self-care is part of motherhood ?

How did becoming a mother change Naomi Osaka’s view of tennis?

Why are boundaries so important to Osaka as a mother?

What can mothers learn from Naomi Osaka’s mental-health journey?

For Naomi Osaka, becoming a mother did not mean putting her own needs aside. Instead, it changed the way she thinks about self-care, mental health and life. The four-time Grand Slam champion, who has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure, has shared a simple but powerful message: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter. ” Her words show why looking after yourself can also be an important part of being a good mother.Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai, with rapper Cordae. Her journey into motherhood came during a major change in her life. She had stepped away from tennis for more than a year and was also trying to understand what she wanted from her career and her life.For Osaka, self-care is not about putting herself before her daughter. It is about making sure she is in a good place so she can also be there for her child.In her conversations about motherhood and mental health, Osaka has spoken about setting boundaries, taking time for herself and paying attention to what she needs. That can mean taking a quiet moment, meditating, getting enough rest when possible or simply saying no when something feels like too much.Her message also pushes back against the idea that mothers must always put themselves last.Being a mother does not mean a woman has to ignore her own feelings, needs or identity.Osaka’s approach is simple. A mother can love her child deeply and still need time for herself. In fact, taking care of her own mental and emotional health can help her be more present for her child.Tennis had been a huge part of Osaka’s life for years. She became world No. 1 and won four Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2018 and the Australian Open in 2019, 2021 and 2022.But success also came with pressure. Osaka made headlines in 2021 when she withdrew from the French Open after explaining that media duties were affecting her mental health. She later stepped away from tennis for an extended period.Becoming a mother gave her another chance to look at her life from a different point of view.Osaka returned to professional tennis in January 2024 after giving birth. The comeback was not easy. She had to rebuild her body, return to the demands of professional sport and deal with the normal ups and downs of competition.But motherhood also helped her understand that tennis was only one part of who she was.Winning was still important to her, but it was no longer the only thing that defined her. She could be a tennis player, a mother and her own person at the same time.That change in thinking also helped Osaka become more open about her emotions. Instead of feeling that she always had to appear strong, she became more comfortable talking about difficult moments and asking for support.Osaka has spent much of her career in the public eye. Her matches, interviews and personal life have all received huge attention. That level of attention can be difficult for anyone, and motherhood has given her even more reason to protect her private life and mental space.She has spoken about how hard it once was for her to say no because she worried about disappointing people. Over time, she learned that she could not make everyone happy and did not have to accept every demand placed on her.That lesson became an important part of how she approaches motherhood.For Osaka, boundaries can mean choosing when to work, taking time away from social media, protecting family time or simply refusing to take on something that could leave her overwhelmed.These choices are not about shutting people out. They are about knowing when she needs to step back.Her experience also sends an important message to other mothers. Saying no does not mean you care less. Taking a break does not mean you are lazy. Asking someone for help does not mean you have failed.Sometimes, protecting your own peace is what allows you to give more of yourself to the people you love.Perhaps the biggest lesson from Osaka’s story is that mental health should not be treated as something people have to hide.She has spoken openly about anxiety, pressure and the challenges that came with being a top athlete. She has also talked about wanting her daughter to grow up in an environment where talking about feelings is normal.Osaka has encouraged the idea that children should be able to express themselves, ask for help and understand their emotions. She has also talked about simple habits such as meditation, quiet time and spending meaningful time with family.For her, these lessons are not only things she can tell her daughter. They are things she can show her through her own actions.When a mother rests when she needs to, she shows her child that rest is important. When she talks about her feelings, she shows that emotions are normal. When she asks for help, she teaches her child that nobody has to deal with everything alone.That may be one of the most important parts of Osaka’s message.Motherhood does not have to mean losing yourself. A woman can still have dreams, a career, friendships, personal goals and time for herself while being a loving and devoted mother.Osaka’s journey shows that self-care is not about choosing yourself instead of your child. It is about making sure you are also cared for.For the tennis star, that balance has become part of the mother she wants to be. Her words, “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter,” capture that idea in the simplest way. Taking care of yourself is not taking love away from your child. Sometimes, it is what helps you give that love with more patience, energy and presence.
Article Summary: Tennis star Naomi Osaka reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting. Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai. The four-time Grand Slam champion has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure.

Mojang is keeping the content pipeline flowing in Minecraft, and the excitement amongst the community is at an all-time high. The next major update is the Third Drop of 2026, and they have yet to reveal the official name for it.It is shaping up to be one of the cosiest and most exploration-friendly updates the game has received in recent memory. It will bring a lot of things, including a brand new biome, a new wood set, furniture blocks, and a brand new structure to discover.Below we have all the details you need to know about the Minecraft Third Drop 2026.The Third Drop 2026 is an upcoming game drop that features dappled forests, abandoned camps, the poplar wood set, wool slabs and stairs, cushions, straw beds, and concrete slabs and stairs.Mojang is testing all the features through the snapshots, and players have already been able to experience most of them.The headline addition of the Third Drop is an entirely new overworld biome. The dappled forest consists of poplar trees with orange, yellow, and red leaves, as well as dirt blocks covered with leaf litter, new red shrubs, and brown mushrooms. After the Chaos Cubed drop took players deep underground, it is a breath of fresh air to have a brand-new destination to discover on the surface.The addition of poplar trees also brings a new wood set, which is a warm grey colour when broken down into planks and slabs. The poplar wood set comes in red, orange, and yellow leaf colors, and poplar saplings can be sold by wandering traders. It is a beautiful addition to the game's palette that builders in particular are going to go absolutely wild for.Scattered through the dappled forest are abandoned camps. They are small structures built from wool stairs and featuring chests or barrels to loot, with a tent-like visual design that fits the woodland explorer fantasy the biome is clearly going for. Having a lootable point of interest in a forest biome gives survival players an actual reason to push into unfamiliar territory.Even better, some abandoned camps contain maps hidden inside their chests. These maps lead to other abandoned camps or various other types of structures in the Overworld, making exploration feel genuinely rewarding in a way that few Minecraft updates have managed before.The drop also brings wool stairs, wool slabs, and wool cushions. Cushions in particular give players a genuine seat block, and pairing them with straw beds gives interiors a soft, homey layer that Minecraft's blocky palette has always struggled to deliver without workarounds.Straw beds are a new bed variant that lets players sleep through the night without changing their spawn point. They can only be used once and will be destroyed after use, and cannot be used in the Nether or the End.It is an elegant solution for players who want to skip the night on long expeditions without permanently shifting their respawn location.Concrete slabs and stairs have also been added as part of the final batch of features from the third drop, rounding out a building-focused update that is sure to keep the community's creative side busy for months to come.The Third Drop 2026 will certainly be pretty exciting to see when it arrives.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “She’s my everything. I love her” How Tom Brady’s mother Galynn defied cancer and stood by the star QB through adversity and his historic Super Bowl comeback
Article Text:
How Tom Brady’s mother Galynn defied cancer and stood by the star QB through adversity and his historic Super Bowl comeback(Getty)

How Galynn Brady ’s cancer diagnosis changed the family’s 2016 season

How Tom Brady supported his mother while facing his own adversity

How Galynn Brady fought through treatment with one goal in mind

How Super Bowl LI became Galynn Brady victory too

Why Robert Kraft gave Galynn Brady her own Super Bowl ring

How Galynn Brady recovery brought another reason for Tom Brady’s family to celebrate

How Galynn’s strength became part of Tom Brady’s story

Success stories are often remembered through championships and records, but Tom Brady’s 2016 season also came with a difficult time for his family. While Brady served a four-game suspension, his mother, Galynn, was undergoing treatment for stage 2 breast cancer, including chemotherapy and radiation.Unable to attend his regular-season games, Galynn watched from home before making it to Super Bowl LI , where she watched Brady lead the Patriots back from 28-3 to beat Atlanta 34-28. After the victory, Brady said, “She’s my everything. I just love her so much.” Tom Brady's mother, Galynn's cancer battle began in the summer of 2016. In an interview with NFL correspondent Andrea Kremer, she remembered sitting in a doctor's office when she was told that she had breast cancer. Doctors told her it was stage 2, but she also learned that the cancer was fast-growing and aggressive.“I just remember sitting in the doctor’s office and them telling me ‘You have breast cancer. It’s only stage 2,’” Galynn recalled. “And so the journey began.”That journey involved five months of chemotherapy, followed by radiation and other treatment. The diagnosis immediately changed the family's routine because Galynn had traditionally been a regular presence at Tom's games.During the 2016 season, however, her health prevented her from travelling to Patriots games.Instead, football became something she watched from home while concentrating on treatment. Her husband, Tom Brady Sr., later explained how the family structured its weeks around Galynn's chemotherapy and Tom's games.“Everything centered around 10 o'clock Thursday morning” for her chemotherapy and then Sunday morning when the family would watch football, he explained. Even while dealing with cancer, Galynn continued following her son's season. Those Sunday games gave the family a familiar routine during months that were anything but normal.Galynn's illness was not the only major challenge facing the Brady family that season. Tom entered 2016 dealing with the fallout from the Deflategate controversy and a four-game suspension.For Brady, watching his mother go through cancer treatment while also dealing with his own public struggles was emotionally difficult. Years later, while discussing that period in Man in the Arena, he explained how painful it had been for Galynn to see her son publicly criticised.“I think, personally, that was very difficult for her to see her son kind of raked through the coals like I was,” Brady said.He believed his mother had already been carrying the stress of her own illness, so seeing what was happening to her son added another burden. The family therefore became an important source of support for both Galynn and Tom.During his suspension, Brady spent time with his family at Pebble Beach in California. His ex wife Gisele Bündchen, daughter Vivian, nieces and nephews were also there. Brady later recalled standing on the 18th hole and looking around at the people closest to him while thinking about what really mattered.“Being with my family at a very vulnerable time,” he said, gave him a different perspective.Instead of allowing football to consume every part of his life, Brady recognised that his mother's health and his family's well-being deserved his attention too.As the Patriots' season continued and the team moved closer to another Super Bowl appearance, the Brady family began thinking about whether Galynn would be healthy enough to attend.Tom Brady told his parents that she would be ready for the Super Bowl. According to Tom Brady Sr., the family had calculated that the end of Galynn's five months of chemotherapy would fall about two weeks before the championship game.Galynn completed her final round of chemotherapy on January 12, 2017. But her recovery did not immediately become easy. She developed pneumonia and shingles, leaving her ability to travel to Houston in doubt.Her doctor did not clear her for the trip until one day before the family was scheduled to leave.Galynn could have stayed home after everything she had endured, but she wanted to see her son play.“There’s a special bond between a mother and a son,” Galynn said. “I just wanted to be there for Tommy, and I wanted to be there with our family. Everybody was going to the Super Bowl and I didn’t want to miss that.”Those words explain why reaching Houston meant so much to her. She had spent months watching Tom from home while going through chemotherapy, but she wanted to be beside him and her family when the Patriots reached the biggest game of the season.Her determination also showed how she approached the cancer battle itself. She was not allowing the illness to completely take away the moments she valued most.Galynn finally made it to Houston, but the game itself quickly became another test for the family.The Patriots fell behind the Atlanta Falcons 28-3, leaving New England with a massive deficit to overcome. Galynn watched from the stands as the team struggled, and the situation became so painful that she eventually told her husband she wanted to leave.“I said to Tom, ‘I just want to go home,’” she later recalled. “I was heartbroken for Tommy.”Tom, however, continued fighting. The Patriots gradually erased the deficit and eventually forced overtime. New England completed the comeback with a 34-28 victory, giving Brady his fifth Super Bowl championship and the Patriots the largest comeback in Super Bowl history.For Galynn, the emotion was overwhelming after everything she had experienced.“I’m so glad that I decided I would go and just put cancer aside for that weekend,” she later said. She had made it to Houston despite the complications that had threatened her recovery, and she was there to watch her son produce one of the most remarkable comebacks in NFL history.The Patriots' victory gave the Brady family a moment they would never forget, but Robert Kraft added another deeply personal gesture afterward. The Patriots owner gave Galynn her own Super Bowl ring, recognising her connection to the team's unforgettable championship season. Kraft's gesture acknowledged what she had endured while Tom was leading New England toward the title.For Galynn, the ring represented much more than the Patriots' victory. It was connected to the months of chemotherapy, the health complications, the uncertainty over whether she could travel and the decision to put her illness aside long enough to be there for her son.The Super Bowl did not mark the end of Galynn's recovery, but it was an important milestone. In June 2017, Tom Brady Sr. said that Galynn had finished her cancer treatment about two months earlier and was doing well, playing golf and tennis again.In August, Tom Brady gave another encouraging update, saying his mother was “on the road to recovery” after receiving very positive test results. “She’s doing really well,” Brady said. “Everyone in our family is so happy.”By October, reports said Galynn's latest cancer screening had come back clear, although her cancer carried a high risk of recurrence. She continued to undergo regular testing as part of her follow-up care.Her experience also encouraged her to share a message with other people facing cancer. Galynn said she hoped people could learn from her story and keep a positive attitude rather than giving up hope.“I would hope that they would learn to keep a positive attitude, and not to give up hope,” she said. “Be thankful every day; think about the people that are caring about you.”That is perhaps the most directly inspirational message from Galynn herself, because it came from someone who had actually gone through the treatment she was describing.Galynn had supported Tom long before he became one of the most successful quarterbacks in NFL history. She was there throughout his career and remained one of the people closest to him, but her cancer battle showed just how strong their bond had become.In 2016, both mother and son were facing challenges that demanded patience and resilience. Tom had to deal with suspension and the pressure surrounding his career, while Galynn had to endure chemotherapy, radiation and serious health complications.Neither could simply remove the other's struggle, but they continued encouraging each other.Tom's support was important to Galynn during treatment, especially when she struggled with the physical changes brought by chemotherapy. She later recalled losing her hair and wearing a bandanna, while Tom would reassure her by telling her she looked beautiful.Galynn, meanwhile, gave Tom another reason to keep pushing when the Patriots faced their biggest challenge of the season.Her decision to travel to Houston brought their two journeys together. She had fought through cancer treatment to be there, and Tom responded with one of the greatest performances of his career.That is what makes Galynn Brady's story so powerful. She was not simply watching her son play football while recovering from cancer. She was actively fighting her own battle, trying to stay positive and refusing to let the illness take away the moments she wanted to share with her family. Tom Brady's Super Bowl LI comeback will always be remembered for the 28-3 deficit, the overtime victory and another championship for one of the NFL's greatest quarterbacks.For the Brady family, however, the night carried a much deeper meaning.Galynn had fought through cancer to sit in those stands. Tom had fought through his own adversity to lead the Patriots back. When the two finally embraced after the victory, the moment represented everything they had endured together.
Article Summary: Tom Brady's mother, Galynn, was diagnosed with breast cancer in the summer of 2016. She underwent five months of chemotherapy, followed by radiation and other treatment. Brady watched from home before making it to Super Bowl LI, where she watched Brady lead the Patriots back from 28-3 to beat Atlanta.
